# Vortex RPG client

TypeScript + PixiJS v8 client of the Habbo RPG fork. It started as a full port of the Habbo Flash
client and is being restructured into standalone packages: read
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-07-client-architecture-design.md` before structural work, and the
plan of the current milestone in `docs/superpowers/plans/`. The server is `../vortex-rpg-emulator`.

## Commands

```bash
pnpm install                 # dependencies (pnpm 11, Node >= 22)
pnpm dev                     # client dev server on :5173 (also starts the imager on :8081)
pnpm check                   # typecheck client+engine+glaze+imager, then all tool tests (~45 s): the gate
pnpm typecheck               # just the typecheck
pnpm test                    # node:test over packages/*/tools and .claude/scripts, then packages/*/test/*.test.ts via tsx
node --test <file.test.mjs>  # one test file
node node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js <file>   # lint one file
pnpm build                   # production build of the client (tsc + vite)
pnpm gen:headers             # regenerate message ids from the emulator's Headers.cs
pnpm sync:agents             # regenerate AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions.md from this file + rules
node install.mjs             # unpack assets (vortex-client-assets.zip); --pack to rebuild the zip
pnpm --filter vortex-client build:pack <dir of .nitro> <out.ambreia>   # lossless .ambreia pack (see rules/assets.md)
```

## Done means verified

1. `pnpm check` is green, and you show its last lines. A Stop hook runs it anyway when the session
   changed `.ts` files, and blocks while it is red.
2. A visible change is looked at: use the `run-vortex-client` skill and compare screenshots.
3. A wire change matches the emulator's serializer/parser for that message.
4. Say what you did not verify. "Should work" is not a result.

## Map

| Package | What it is |
|---|---|
| `packages/ambreia-common` | `@ambreia/common`: Logger, utilities, asset loading (incl. `.ambreia` packs: `assets/pack/`), reactive — imports no other Ambreia package |
| `packages/ambreia-net` | `@ambreia/net`: WebSocket transport, encryption, wire format, registry, packet tap, the new message style (`style/MessageMap`) — imports `@ambreia/common` only |
| `packages/ambreia-avatar` | `@ambreia/avatar`: avatar renderer (not the editor), built from typed options; runs in Node (`tools/render-avatar.mjs`) — imports `@ambreia/common` only |
| `packages/ambreia-ui` | `@ambreia/ui`: window system (`src/`), generic kit (`src/kit/`: plain `WindowManager`, `WidgetRegistry`, dialogs, generic widgets), XML parsers (`src/assets/`); `pnpm --filter @ambreia/ui sandbox` shows it alone — imports `@ambreia/common` only |
| `packages/ambreia-kernel` | `@ambreia/kernel`: DI (`runtime/`), typed config (`config/`: Zod, `app` + `legacy` + one section per feature, `config.json`), features (`feature/`: `defineFeature`, `bootFeatures`) — imports `@ambreia/common` only |
| `packages/ambreia-iso` | `@ambreia/iso`: room engine — core (`src/`), `scene/`, `furniture/`, `avatar/`, `effects/`, each with its `register*` module; `IsoStage` loads a room out of session (zone format); `pnpm --filter @ambreia/iso sandbox` — imports `@ambreia/common` and `@ambreia/avatar` only |
| `packages/ambreia-protocol` | `@ambreia/protocol`: `Headers.generated.ts` (from the emulator), `HabboMessages.ts`, the inherited messages, parsers and composers — imports `@ambreia/common`, `net`, `iso` only |
| `packages/ambreia-game` | `@ambreia/game`: the game over the engines — `features/` (`GAME_FEATURES`, `IGameFeature`: images, room widgets; one folder per feature, e.g. `loading-bar/`), `core/` (DI wrappers), `avatar` incl. the editor, `communication`, `configuration`, `localization`, `room` (RoomEngine, the message handler: the glue over `iso`), `session`, `ui` (room desktop, `RoomWidgetRegistry`), `window` (`HabboWindowManager extends WindowManager`), `iid/` — never imports the host packages |
| `packages/vortex-engine` | The host shell: `Vortex`, `VortexMain` (boots `GAME_FEATURES` through the kernel), their interfaces |
| `packages/vortex-client` | App shell: boot (`src/App.ts`), display classes, assets, `src/vortex-layouts/` (new window XML) |
| `packages/vortex-glaze` | Live window-layout editor — imports `@ambreia/ui` and `@ambreia/common` only (ESLint wall) |
| `packages/vortex-imager` | Server-side avatar/furni/room renderer reusing the engine |

The project is named **Ambreia** (the MMORPG); new packages take the `@ambreia/` scope, the older
`vortex-*` names are renamed in a later pass. `@ambreia/common/*` and `@ambreia/net/*` are workspace
packages imported by deep path (`@ambreia/common/utils/Logger`; a folder barrel is `…/utils/index`);
`packages/vortex-engine/tools/move-modules.mjs` moves files into a package and rewrites their imports.
Browser globals (canvas, image decode, XML) go through `platform()` of `@ambreia/common/platform/Platform`;
a Node tool calls `setPlatform()` first (see `packages/ambreia-avatar/tools/node-platform.mjs`). Engine
packages are plain classes; the DI registers them with `context.attachInstance(iid, instance, {dependencies, ready, update})`.
`@ambreia/ui` (the package) is not `@ui/` (the client's alias for its own `src/`).
Aliases: in the client `@ui/` and `@/` → client `src/` (the engine's `@core/` `@habbo/` `@iid/` went with J6:
import `@ambreia/game/…`). Target: engines become packages `@vortex/common`, `net`, `avatar`, `iso`, `ui`, then `kernel`,
`protocol`, `game` (spec §3, milestones J1–J6).

## Never

- **Edit `sources/**`, `*.generated.ts`, built `src/assets/window-*` or `.vortex-dev/`.** A hook refuses
  and names what to run instead.
- **Cross a layer wall**: engines (`common`, `net`, `avatar`, `iso`, `ui`) never import `kernel`,
  `protocol` or `game`; nothing under `packages/ambreia-*` imports a `vortex-*` package; the game's
  `core/` never reaches out of `core/`. ESLint enforces it (`wall()` in `eslint.config.mjs`); an
  error there means the design is wrong, not the rule.
- **Type a message id**: use `Incoming.X` / `Outgoing.X` from `Headers.generated.ts`.
- **Run a bare `git commit`**: the owner keeps staged work in progress. Commit by path:
  `git commit -m "…" -- <paths>`.
- **Override `get events()` in a `Component` subclass**: it breaks DI events (use another name, e.g.
  `sessionEvents`).
- **Re-port a removed feature** (RPG spec §7: wired, Builders Club, NFT, …), nor a hotel module the
  core cut removed (catalog, inventory, navigator, messenger, friends, groups, help, moderation,
  quests, toolbar, notifications, sound, the fishing derby…). A new feature is written for the RPG; the old code is under
  the git tag `pre-noyau-client` for reading. The network contract is the 60 messages in
  `HabboMessages.ts`, aligned on the server.

## Conventions ESLint does not check

- `dispose()` is the last method of a class and returns early when `_disposed` is already set.
- Log with `Logger.getLogger('habbo.room.RoomEngine')`: `trace` per frame/packet/item, `debug` for a
  subsystem's own commentary, `info` for milestones, `warn` for data or paths the client does not
  handle (they render nothing, so `debug` would hide them), `error` when the user will notice.
- A manager is a feature (`@ambreia/game/features/`, one line in `GAME_FEATURES`; a new feature gets its own folder):
  a DI `Component` or a plain instance under an IID, with one `I<Manager>` interface (`docs/PATTERNS.md`).
  Config: a feature reads its own section; old keys go through `legacy` / `getProperty` until migrated.
- Render loops allocate nothing per frame and use `Set`/`Map` for lookups (`docs/STYLEGUIDE.md` →
  Performance).
- Comments are in English and say why. Inherited code keeps its `// AS3:` trace when moved
  (`.claude/rules/30-as3-traceability.md`).

## Before you change inherited code

- **Read the body of every call you remove, replace or stop making**, not its name. Names come from
  the AS3 and the TS behind them often does something else: `createMainWindow()` ended with
  `hideMainWindow()`, which detaches the window rather than hiding it; replacing it with
  `visible = false` stopped the catalog from opening at all.
- **"This change is inert" is a claim, not an observation.** Verify it before writing it.
- **A finding from an audit or an agent is a claim.** In one audit, 3 of 26 "criticals" were wrong
  and one fix would have broken the client. Re-check against the code before acting.
- **When a correct change misbehaves, suspect the structure under it** before reverting the change.

## Keeping this file useful

Keep it under ~150 lines: it loads in every session. Add a line only after the same mistake happens
twice, and prefer a lint rule, hook or test when the rule can be checked. Anything that applies to
part of the repo goes in a path-scoped `.claude/rules/*.md`. `AGENTS.md` is generated: run
`pnpm sync:agents` after editing this file or a rule (the pre-commit hook checks it).

## Rule: AS3 traces and inherited code

_Applies to: `packages/*/src/**/*.ts`_

Inherited code carries a trace to its AS3 origin immediately above the declaration:

```ts
// AS3: sources/WIN63-202607011411-782849652/src/com/sulake/<path>/<Class>.as::<member>()
```

Since 2026-10-07 the trace is **provenance, not a fidelity contract** (client architecture spec §10).

- **Keep the `AS3:` line when you move, rename or restructure a member.** It is the only pointer to
  the code that explains the behaviour. It always names the primary tree and a readable member name,
  never a `_SafeStr_N`/`_SafeCls_N` placeholder.
- **A member that now behaves differently keeps its trace.** Add `// DEVIATION: <what AS3 did, why
  this differs>` when the difference would surprise someone reading the AS3.
- **A half-done inherited member** keeps a compatible signature and `// TODO(AS3): <path>::<member>,
  <what remains>`.
- **New code takes no marker.** `// TS-only: <reason>` is only for a member added to a class that was
  ported from the AS3.

## A faithful line is not a faithful behaviour

When changing inherited code, read further than the line: the rest of the method, the callee it
assigns through, and whoever feeds the value. Four shapes account for every such bug found so far:

1. **Same line, different data.** `-offset.x` was right for a Flash library `<offset>`; the Nitro
   spritesheet path already stores `offsetX = -assetDef.x`. Check what feeds a value before copying
   arithmetic on it.
2. **The languages differ.** `for each` over `undefined` iterates nothing in AS3; `for...of` throws.
   `getString()` never returns null here, so an AS3 `!= null` presence test becomes `hasString()`.
   `x || 1` destroys a legitimate `0`. AS3 runs a subclass's field initialisers before `super()`.
3. **Half-ported contract.** `sprite.assetName = name` matched the AS3, which also set `.asset` on the
   next line. `WindowToolTipAgent` reads `inputEventQueue.mouseX`, but the port never enqueues, so it
   reads zero.
4. **AS3 bugs Flash masked.** `ContextInfoView` calls `show()` outside the branch that positions it.
   Keep the behaviour, note the discrepancy at the declaration, say which one you kept.

## Rule: Reading the AS3 sources

_Applies to: `sources/**`, `**/*.as`_

`sources/` holds decompiled Flash client dumps. They are read-only reference (a hook refuses edits):
read them to understand why inherited code behaves as it does. Since 2026-10-07 the port no longer
has to stay faithful to them, and **message ids never come from them** (the emulator's `Headers.cs` is
the source, via `pnpm gen:headers`).

## The trees

| Directory                                    | Use                    | Package roots                           |
|----------------------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `sources/WIN63-202607011411-782849652/`      | **Primary**            | `src/com/sulake/{habbo,room,core,iid}/` |
| `sources/win63_version/`                     | Names only             | `habbo/`, `room/`, `core/`              |
| `sources/PRODUCTION-201601012205-226667486/` | Identify / recover names (2016, unobfuscated) | `src/com/sulake/habbo/` |
| `sources/AIR-1.0.31/`                        | Behaviour of AIR-only features, never ids | `src/com/sulake/{habbo,room,core,iid}/` |

Path mapping: `WIN63-…/src/com/sulake/<module>/` ↔ `win63_version/<module>/` ↔
`PRODUCTION-…/src/com/sulake/habbo/<module>/`. `AS3:` trace comments always point at the primary tree.

## Obfuscation

- **Class names are obfuscated, member names are not.** `habbo/room/_SafeCls_90.as` declares
  `implements IRoomEngine` and its 255 methods are readable: that file is RoomEngine. Identify a class
  by the interface it implements, not by a name lookup.
- **About 40% of interfaces are obfuscated too** (`implements _SafeCls_1783` says nothing until that
  interface is resolved). Match its members against a named interface in PRODUCTION, or against this
  port's own `I*.ts` (`_SafeCls_1783` is `ICatalogNavigator`, because `CatalogNavigator.as` takes it).
- **When a name exists in no tree, derive it and say so at the declaration**; never pass a derived
  name off as recovered (see `CatalogWindowState.requestedPage`).
- `win63_version` does **not** recover names file-for-file: it is obfuscated with another scheme
  (RoomEngine is `_SafeCls_90.as` in the primary, `class_34.as` there, `RoomEngine.as` only in PRODUCTION).

## `win63_version` is a worse decompile: never read a body from it

Its bodies have produced shipped bugs: `SpinnerCatalogWidget.refresh()` reads `visible = 0 > 0` (a
permanently hidden container); `GiftWrappingConfigurationEventParser.parse()` reads `while(0 < _loc2_)`
in four loops (a browser hang). When a `win63_version` body reads as dead or absurd, it is the
decompiler and the primary tree settles it. Cite `win63_version` only for a *name* (it is the only
tree where messages have readable filenames).

## Decompiler traps in the primary tree

- **E4X `@` is dropped from computed attribute access.** `_loc3_.@["order-before"]` comes back as
  `_loc3_["order-before"]`, which reads as child access and makes live code look dead. If the name is
  an attribute in the XML, the source had `.@[...]` (`AvatarModelGeometry.as`, `order-before`).
- **`src/unknowns/` (`_SafePkg_N/`) is part of the client**: 556 files import from it (parser DTOs,
  composers, `IStuffData` holders). Search it before concluding a definition does not exist.
- **The flat `src/_SafeCls_N.as` files are the embedded-asset classes** and carry the name mapping in
  a footer comment (`@identifier _SafeCls_894 = "header_png$e4f111fb..."`); `tools/lib/cryptedManifest.mjs`
  reads them.

## AIR-1.0.31

A later build and a strict superset in readable classes. It is the only tree with **VariableFx**
(`habbo/room/object/variablefx/`, `.../visualization/variablefx/`, `.../visualization/stacked/`),
**raid protection** (`habbo/navigator/raidprotection/`) and the wired `VariablesWebApiAddon`. Read it
for behaviour of those. Its assets are 1,092 `.bin` blobs in `src/binaryData/` named
`<charId>_<class>`, where `<class>` is the linkage name or the `_SafeCls_N` its `*Com.as` assigns:
`HabboNavigatorCom.as` says `raid_protection_settings_xml:Class = _SafeCls_1412`, so the layout is
`binaryData/3129__SafeCls_1412.bin`. **Look there before reconstructing an AIR layout by hand.** Images
are not in the dump: cut them from the launcher's `HabboAir.swf` with JPEXS
(`ffdec-cli -export binaryData,symbolClass,image <outdir> <swf>`), then
`AIR_IMAGE_EXPORT=<dir> node packages/vortex-client/tools/import-air-images.mjs`.

## Not this project's server

`sources/HABBO-ARCTURUS-DAYBREAK/` is an unrelated Java emulator from a 2016 build: 221 of its 229
shared message names disagree on the id. Read it only to see how someone else serialised a message.

## Rule: Client assets: how they are built and named

_Applies to: `packages/vortex-client/tools/**`, `packages/vortex-client/src/assets/**`, `packages/vortex-glaze/tools/**`, `install.mjs`_

- **Window layouts and skins ship as XML, verbatim from the dump**, written by
  `packages/vortex-client/tools/build-window-assets.mjs` out of the dump's `src/layouts/` +
  `src/_assets/` + `src/binaryData/*Com.as`. There is no JSON compile step. `binaryDataXml_organized/`
  is a leftover named after each XML's internal `<layout name="...">`, a Flash label AS3 never reads:
  name nothing from it. New, non-Habbo layouts go in `packages/vortex-client/src/vortex-layouts/`.
- **An asset's real name is its `*Com.as` field name**, the exact string passed to
  `assets.getAssetByName()` (`HabboWindowManagerCom.as`: `habbo_window_layout_bubble_xml:Class =
  bubble_xml$44e3d739...`). Libraries are per component, so one field name can mean two embeds
  (`avatar_image_xml` in HabboFriendBar and HabboWindowManager): join declarations to files on the
  embed's **whole** linkage name, hash included. Collapsing to the short name once shipped a layout
  under an image's name.
- **The builder also reads AIR-1.0.31 as a supplement.** `resolveTree()` tells the two tree shapes
  apart by where the `*Com.as` manifests are, never by directory name. AIR adds names WIN63 lacks and
  never replaces one, except the names in `AIR_PREFERRED` (today: adds `raid_protection_settings_xml`,
  overrides `iro_room_details_framed_xml`). `--no-air` builds without it. Measure AIR-vs-WIN63 gaps
  with the builder's own report, not by filename: AIR blobs carry linkage names, shipped assets carry
  field names.
- **Images are gitignored** (`*.png`). A new image reaches anyone else only through
  `vortex-client-assets.zip` (`node install.mjs --pack`). Image names keep their subfolder under
  `images/` (`images/rpg/skills/icon_00.png` → `rpg/skills/icon_00`).
- `import-air-images.mjs` reads AIR's `*Com.as` **and `*Lib.as`** (VariableFx art is declared in
  `HabboRoomObjectVisualizationLib.as`) and strips a redundant `_png` suffix from field names
  (`user_typing_png` is the shipped `user_typing.png`).
- **Shipped assets can lag the primary dump**: check before assuming a code gap.
  `src/assets/configurations/HabboAvatarGeometry.xml` has 9 bodyparts and no `order-*` attributes
  where the WIN63 dump has 11 (`petl`/`petr`).
- **`.ambreia` packs stand in for directories of `.nitro`** (plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-08-asset-packs.md`).
  `build-asset-pack.ts` writes one (lossless WebP checked per pixel, manifests through
  `ManifestCodec`, a full read-back; unreadable bundles listed in `<pack>.report.json`). The
  `asset-packs` feature mounts `config.json` → `asset-packs.{clothing,furniture}` on the avatar /
  furniture download directories; `NitroBundleLoader` reads a mounted piece with one HTTP Range and
  falls back to the `.nitro` when the pack lacks it or the server ignores Range. Image *data* is
  identical; browsers premultiply PNG and WebP alpha with different rounding, so semi-transparent
  pixels can render ±1/255 apart.

## Rule: Wire protocol / communication rules

_Applies to: `**/communication/**`, `packages/ambreia-net/**`, `packages/ambreia-protocol/**`_

You are editing wire-protocol code (`packages/ambreia-net/` — transport, encryption, wire format,
registry, the new style's `style/MessageMap` — `packages/ambreia-protocol/` — `Headers.generated.ts`,
`HabboMessages.ts` and the inherited messages, parsers and composers — or the game's
`communication/`, the managers that use them).

The server is **`../vortex-rpg-emulator`** (C#, Orleans). Its wire contract is
`Vortex.Revisions/Revision20260701/`: `Headers.cs` (ids), `Parsers/` (what it reads from us),
`Serializers/` (what it sends us), `Maps/` (which header goes with which). That repo is the
authority on every message; `sources/HABBO-ARCTURUS-DAYBREAK/` is not this project's server.

1. Read `docs/CLIENT-SERVER-ARCHITECTURE.md` for the flow you are touching (handshake/encryption, or the request-response of that message) before changing anything here.
2. Code that looks wrong (odd byte order, a seemingly redundant field) may compensate for a documented server behaviour: check that document's "known server bugs and protocol mismatches" list, then the emulator's serializer, before "fixing" it.
3. `Parser.parse()` read order and `Composer.getMessageArray()` field order MUST match the emulator's serializer/parser for that message (`vortex-rpg-emulator/Vortex.Revisions/Revision20260701/{Serializers,Parsers}/`); reordering silently breaks the wire format.
4. See `docs/PATTERNS.md` → MessageComposer / MessageParser / MessageEvent templates before adding a new message type. Quick shape reminder:
   - **Composer**: `extends MessageComposer<TupleType>` with `_data` and `getMessageArray()`
   - **Parser**: `implements IMessageParser` with `flush()` + `parse(wrapper)`
   - **Event**: `extends MessageEvent implements IMessageEvent` with `callback` parameter in constructor
5. **Message ids come from `Headers.generated.ts`**, written by `pnpm gen:headers` from the emulator's `Headers.cs` and checked by the pre-commit hook. New registrations use `Incoming.X` / `Outgoing.X`; never type an id by hand, never take one from the AS3 registry.
6. **A new message uses the new style** (spec §6, `@ambreia/net/style/MessageMap`): a plain class, an
   `IIncomingParser` or `IOutgoingSerializer`, an `IMessageHandler`, and a `MessageMap` per domain
   installed on the connection (`map.install(connection)`, `map.send(connection, message)`). A header
   an inherited event already serves is refused at install: take it out of `HabboMessages` and add
   it to `@ambreia/protocol/NewStyleHeaders` (the registration tests accept either style, never both).

## Rule: Room engine rules

_Applies to: `**/room/**`, `packages/ambreia-iso/**`_

`@ambreia/iso` is the room engine: its core (`src/`: manager, instances, objects, renderer, events, utils), `scene/` (planes, content loader, factories), `furniture/`, `avatar/`, `effects/` — a type is drawn only if its module registered it (`registerScene/Furniture/Avatars/Effects`, `DEFAULT_ROOM_MODULES`). `@ambreia/game`'s `room/` keeps the game glue (`RoomEngine`, `RoomMessageHandler`). Out of session, rooms load through `IsoStage`.

1. Use `createObjectInternal()`, never `createRoomObject()`, when creating room objects from a container (the latter recurses infinitely).
2. `renderer/` is a render-loop hot path: no allocations per frame, cache textures by content key, cull objects outside the viewport. See `docs/STYLEGUIDE.md` → Performance.
3. See `docs/PATTERNS.md` for Manager/Handler patterns before adding new room object types.
4. A new room object type is a `register()` in its module's `register*.ts`, not a `switch` case; effects (avatar additions, particles) go through `AvatarVisualization.additions` / `FurnitureFireworksVisualization.particleSystems`, set by `registerEffects`.

## Rule: `pnpm dev` pre-bundles the engine

_Applies to: `packages/vortex-client/vite.config.ts`, `packages/vortex-client/tools/vite-plugin-*.mjs`, `packages/*/package.json`_

The client statically reaches ~3,970 of the engine's files at boot; served one request per module
that was 15 s cold and ~6 s per reload (the port has no `import.meta.hot`, so every change is a full
reload). `tools/vite-plugin-engine-bundle.mjs` hands the engine to esbuild in watch mode instead
(~185 requests, ~1.3 s cold, ~0.45 s reload). It is serve-only; `pnpm build` is untouched.

- **One esbuild graph covers the engine and the workspace packages** (`@ambreia/common`,
  `@ambreia/net`, `ui`, `avatar`, `iso`…; `outbase` is `packages/`), so their singletons (`Logger`, `FrameTimings`) exist once.
  Every `packages/ambreia-*/src` is found on disk (`workspaceAliases()`) and any `@ambreia/<name>`
  specifier is routed to the bundle, so a new package needs no edit; one served by Vite instead would
  be a second copy.

- **No `@ambreia/*` or engine alias in `resolve.alias`.** `vite:alias` runs before user
  `enforce: 'pre'` plugins, so an alias would rewrite the specifier to source before the plugin sees
  it, and the ~3,970 requests come back. A build takes the packages from the workspace links. The
  old `@core`/`@habbo`/`@iid` aliases went with J6 (`@ambreia/game`).
- **Only `pixi.js` and `eventemitter3` are external to the bundle** (the client imports them too and
  there must be one instance). `pako` is engine-only and not resolvable from the client package:
  externalising it gives "Failed to resolve import" and a blank page.
- The bundle is written to `packages/vortex-client/.vortex-dev/` (gitignored, ESLint-ignored, and a
  hook refuses edits there).

## Rule: UI / window system rules

_Applies to: `**/window/**`, `**/widgets/**`, `packages/ambreia-ui/**`_

You are editing the ported Flash UI/window system: `@ambreia/ui` (`packages/ambreia-ui/src`, its generic kit in `src/kit/`), the game windows in `@ambreia/game`'s `window/` and `*/widgets/`, and the client's `window/`.

1. See `docs/PATTERNS.md` → "UI Window (ported from Flash)" and "Component Lifecycle" for the expected class shape. Quick shape reminder: UI Windows are ported from the AS3 `IWindow`/`IFrameWindow` hierarchy using PixiJS + the XML layouts described in rule 3.
2. Never override `get events()` in a Component subclass — it breaks the DI event system. Use a differently named property (e.g. `sessionEvents`).
3. Flash XML layouts and skins ship **as XML**, verbatim from the AS3 asset library (`vortex-client/src/assets/window-layouts`, `window-skins`), and are parsed at runtime by `WindowXmlAssetParser` — do not reintroduce a JSON compile step. `tools/build-window-assets.mjs` is the only tool that writes those two directories; it names every file after the `*Com.as` field that declares it, which is the exact string AS3 passes to `assets.getAssetByName()`. Never name an asset after the XML's own `<layout name="...">`: that is a Flash-authoring label AS3 never reads.
4. Flash UI windows/dialogs (`IWindow`, `IFrameWindow`, etc.) are ported as TypeScript classes using PixiJS; Flash display components (buttons, text fields, scrollbars, etc.) are ported as PixiJS display objects. Preserve the original AS3 class hierarchy for UI — do not collapse it into a simplified component model.
5. **A layout declares its own images. Filling one from code is the exception, not the default.** A `<static_bitmap>` names its image with `<var key="asset_uri" value="fishingUI_bg" type="String"/>` in its `<variables>` block — 293 shipped layouts do this. `WindowParser` reads the key and hands it to `StaticBitmapWrapperController.assetUri`, which resolves it through the `ResourceManager`; every image in the bundle is registered under its bare filename (no `.png`), so a bare name works. `properties` round-trips the key, so the image survives an edit-and-save in **vortex-glaze** — which is the point: a layout built out of code-filled `<bitmap>` nodes shows as empty slots there and cannot be laid out. Reach for a plain `<bitmap>` only when the pixels are *computed* (a per-frame composite); two-state art is a second `static_bitmap` underneath toggled by `visible`, the idiom `Achievement.xml` uses. Note the mechanism is on `static_bitmap` only — `<bitmap>` has no image attribute, and `BitmapWrapperController.bitmapAssetName` is written by code and read by nothing.
6. **Text alignment is `auto_size`, and it is a string.** `<var key="auto_size" value="center" type="String"/>` — the values are `left` / `center` / `right` / `none`, not a boolean, and 492 shipped layouts use `center`. `TextSkinRenderer` shifts the line by `(maxWidth - textWidth) / 2`. There is no `align` attribute, which is what makes this easy to miss: do not hand-place a label's x to fake centring, because the glyph width changes with the font and with the text.
